subject: Physics
title: The SI System: Seven Base Units
summary: In 1999 NASA lost the Mars Climate Orbiter because one team used pound-force and another newtons. Why the world uses one system, the SI, built on seven base units.

notes.title: 01 – The SI System: Seven Base Units

keyPoints: **Mars Climate Orbiter (1999)** was lost because one team's software gave impulse in pound-force seconds while the navigation team expected newton seconds.
The **SI** (Système International, 1960) is the one system of units used worldwide in science.
It has **seven base units**: metre (m), kilogram (kg), second (s), ampere (A), kelvin (K), mole (mol), candela (cd).
Every other unit is **derived**: newton N = kg m s⁻² (from F = ma), joule J = N m = kg m² s⁻².

quiz.q: How many base units does the SI have?
quiz.explain: m, kg, s, A, K, mol, cd.
